title: Therapeutic Goods Amendment (2013 Measures No. 1) Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would revise therapeutic goods regulation, including powers to exclude products, remove inappropriate register entries, obtain safety information and address misleading regulatory submissions.
It would let the Minister exclude specified products by disallowable instrument and let the Secretary remove products that no longer qualify as therapeutic goods.
Most amendments would begin on Royal Assent, while a separate schedule would start by proclamation or at the end of a six-month fallback period.
changes: The Secretary could require sponsors to notify the public or specified groups about goods in defined regulatory circumstances.
Failure to provide requested information could lead to cancellation of a product's registration or listing.
False or misleading statements supporting a request to vary a register entry would attract new offences and civil penalties.
Merits review of separate product information approval decisions would be removed, while judicial review and review of registration or variation decisions would remain.
summary.affected: Therapeutic goods sponsors, applicants, suppliers, health professionals and patients are affected.

speeches.speaker: Catherine King
speeches.brief: Moved a bill giving the Health Minister power to exclude products such as bacteria-infused mattresses or power band bracelets from regulation as therapeutic goods, allowing the department secretary to remove non-therapeutic products from the register, and creating a new offence for providing false or misleading information when varying a product's registration.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Southcott
speeches.brief: Spoke on the Therapeutic Goods Amendment bill, which would give the minister power to exclude products such as holographic 'power bands' and bacteria-infused mattresses from the therapeutic goods regulatory scheme where public health risk is low, while still leaving them subject to consumer protection law.

speeches.speaker: Shayne Neumann
speeches.brief: Responded that the Therapeutic Goods Amendment bill would harmonise regulatory rules across different classes of therapeutic goods, noting the act's broad definition, unchanged for more than 20 years, increasingly catches products like mattresses and jewellery making health claims.
